document_title: 96 Trillion Cubic Feet, No Way to Market
post_copy:
The USGS counts a mean 96 trillion cubic feet of undiscovered North Slope gas. The same fact sheet says it has no route to market at scale.

Nearest is the reservoir. Most gas raised with oil goes back into it.
Next, near Prudhoe Bay, the North Slope Borough and Twenty First Century Utilities pitch North Slope Power at 3 to 10 gigawatts for AI data centers.
Then STAK Energy, 26 miles south of Deadhorse, where DNR has preliminarily decided to offer a 50-year lease on 715.4 acres for a gas-powered plant with high-performance computing units.
Last in line is Alaska LNG, whose 800-mile pipe to Cook Inlet has no final investment decision.

The USGS count and its 17.3 to 276.7 trillion cubic foot range, reinjected gas, both buyers and the pipe on south-up maps.

Should STAK's lease be signed before Alaska LNG has a final investment decision?

#NorthSlope #AlaskaLNG #AlaskaGas

STAK's location on the map is approximate. DNR gives the acreage and the distance from Deadhorse but not the parcel's shape, so the map draws it as a disc of true area. The Alaska LNG route is a schematic between its two stated ends.
The Alaska AI Docket tracks the state's open AI and energy decisions, each with its next date and primary record, at https://alaskaaihq.com
If you know where DNR's final decision on ADL 422741 stands, or where Alaska LNG's investment decision is headed, add it below.

slides.headline: 96 trillion cubic feet. "No method" to market it.
Counted from the mountains to 3 miles offshore.
slides.body: The USGS mean is 96 trillion cubic feet of gas not yet discovered. The same page says "there is no method for bringing natural gas to markets at large commercial scales."

slides.headline: A risked range, not reserves.
labels: TRILLION CUBIC FEET OF GAS · UNDISCOVERED, TECHNICALLY RECOVERABLE, CONVENTIONAL
DOT DENSITY IS THE CHANCE · GOLD MARKS A ROUTE TO A BUYER, AND THIS PAGE HAS NONE

slides.kicker: PRUDHOE BAY · THE GAS ALREADY FOUND
slides.headline: Even the gas already found goes back down.
slides.body: Most gas that comes up with North Slope oil is pumped back underground to hold reservoir pressure.

slides.headline: The count stops at the mountains. If the gas can't cross them, the buyer comes to the gas.
715.4 acres beside the Dalton, 26 miles south of Deadhorse.
slides.body: DNR's preliminary decision would lease it to STAK Energy for 50 years, for a gas-powered facility with modular high-performance computing units. A gigawatt or more, per the Anchorage Press. More than 500 comments came in.

slides.headline: Pitched as the world's largest gas power plant.
slides.body: North Slope Power, from the North Slope Borough and Twenty First Century Utilities, plans 3 gigawatts first and up to 10, for colocated AI data centers.
labels: SITE GIVEN ONLY AS NEAR PRUDHOE BAY

slides.headline: 800 miles of pipe, still no decision.
slides.body: It would carry North Slope gas to an export terminal on Cook Inlet. Its final investment decision, first proposed for last year, still hasn't been made.

slides.headline: Until a pipe exists, first claim on North Slope gas goes to whoever builds beside it.
slides.body: Should the Legislature decide who gets it first?

aftercare: Post in a Tuesday to Thursday slot, 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time. Tuesday, October 27th is the first such slot after this draft. Drafts arrive daily, and when to post is the owner's call.

Paste the sources comment within 60 seconds of posting, with every raw URL showing as plain text. The two DNR notice links end in id numbers, so click each once after posting to confirm LinkedIn kept the whole link.
Before publishing, check that the PDF document title reads "96 Trillion Cubic Feet, No Way to Market".

Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes. Answer "reserves" misreadings from the record. 96 is undiscovered, technically recoverable gas, the mean of a 17.3 to 276.7 trillion cubic foot range, and Interior puts proven North Slope reserves at roughly 35. STAK has a preliminary decision only, so never describe the lease as approved.
After 48 hours, note saves, comments and reposts for the ledger. Saves count most.
editor_notes_for_email: UPDATE of No.78 (October 5th, More than three Alaskas of power, planned for Prudhoe Bay). New since then are the USGS province-wide count of October 21st with its own sentence that there is no method to bring the gas to market at large commercial scale, STAK Energy's lease 26 miles south of Deadhorse, and Alaska LNG still without a final investment decision. Honesty notes. (1) 96 tcf is undiscovered, technically recoverable, conventional gas, the mean of a risked range, never reserves (C01 to C03, C08). The high case prints as 276.7 because Table 1 reads 276,681 BCFG; the Beacon's 276.6 is a truncation (C02). The 35 tcf proven figure is Interior's and prints PER INTERIOR (C12). (2) STAK's capacity, a gigawatt or more, comes only from the Anchorage Press (C24). DNR's notice says modular high-performance computing units and gives no capacity (C21). Its decision is preliminary (C18). (3) STAK's map location is approximate, a true-area disc at DNR's stated 26 miles south of Deadhorse. (4) The Alaska LNG route on slide 08 is a schematic between its two stated ends (C32). (5) North Slope Power's 3 to 10 gigawatts are the proponents' plans (C28), site given only as near Prudhoe Bay (C30). (6) Trump's post is undated in the record (C31). The caption asks whether STAK's lease should be signed before Alaska LNG's final investment decision; slide 09 asks whether the Legislature should decide who gets the gas first. They point the same way; pick one for replies.
